analysis: This PR adds only documentation: a new changelog.d entry and an edit to the `stop` row of the parameter table in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 2122), plus a date bump on line 3. No executable code, keys, attestation, encryption, authorization, cache-storage or protocol logic changes in the supplied units. The docs describe Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers excluding reasoning and tool-call spans from stop-sequence matching per request (`ReasoningStopScope`). They also say the native block engine (diffusion Gemma) matches the whole output and carries no scope. The reported stop sequence replays the request's scope. I examined these against the threat model (TB-007 inference engine, TB-002 coordinator-provider websocket, A-001 prompts and completions, T-007, T-041). The claimed behavior changes only when a client-supplied stop string ends generation, an availability and output-shaping concern. It does not widen exposure of A-001. Reasoning is still withheld from content, and the claimed change makes stop matching narrower. One residual question is untestable here because the Swift sources (ReasoningStopScope, StopHoldback, EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift) were not supplied. Possible concerns are that stop matching on withheld reasoning could leak reasoning-derived timing or truncation, or that a scope bug could let a stop sequence cut tool-call frames. I cannot confirm the implementation matches the documentation. The doc/changelog text states no new trust boundary, key handling or data flow. No threat-model update appears needed from these documentation edits alone. A later pass should review the actual implementation commit if it is in another batch.
